critical_code_review_comments: index.css has TWO parallel design tokens for teal panels: `.panel-solid-teal/clay/sage` (line 276-298, solid saturated bg + FORCED white text on all descendants via `:not([class*="bg-"])` override) and `.sect-teal/clay/sage` (line 1495-1502, LIGHT-TINT bg + colored inset border, dark ink retained). This dual system is the root cause of the regression the user is polishing: any accidental swap from `.sect-*` to `.panel-solid-*` on a card that has dark-ink descendants will silently whiten all text (h/p/span/li/etc), causing invisible/blended output. Recommend consolidating into a single token with an explicit `data-tone="solid|soft"` attribute so the intent is explicit at every call site.

The automated legibility checker I wrote (contrast walker) has a false-positive pattern when a page has an outer teal SECTION wrapper — text nodes inside a nested white/bg-surface card are reported as sitting on the ancestor teal bg because the walker climbs through transparent parents. For future iterations, prefer testing the RENDERED PIXEL at the text-node bounding-box centre (page.evaluate → getBoundingClientRect + a puppeteer/playwright screenshot pixel-sample) rather than walking CSS ancestors.
